what_happened: The job to require a measured stage timeline in readings of speed requests was rejected at the final verdict. There was one major finding and no blocker. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet, and no checks failed. The new detector (check_speed_timeline / speed_request in reading.rs) reads only the new request text. It ignores attempt.request, which refusing_check already receives. So a bare retry of a speed request is not caught. This is the shape of job 20261025-190606-eebk, one of the three jobs the change claims to fix.
cause: The rule was designed from the wording of the request and not replayed against the cited real cases. A retry carries almost no text of its own, because the original request lives in attempt.request. Nothing requires a new refusal rule to be run against each instance it claims to fix, or to state which inputs it reads. The reading criteria say what the rule should refuse but not that every cited instance must be refused, so a gap for 1 of 3 cited jobs passed until the verifier compared the diff to the cases. Athena already has a replay mechanism for refusal rules, but this job's criteria did not require it per cited instance.
prevention: Add a code check that every job adding or changing a refusal rule must replay the rule over each job id cited in its request, using the same inputs the real flow gives it (new request text plus attempt.request for retries). The check fails the job unless every cited instance is refused or is listed with a stated reason. Run it before the final verdict, so the producer sees a failing case it must fix.
proposed_request: Fix the speed-request timeline refusal so it also covers bare retries. Outcome: a reading of a retry or follow-up whose own text is short, but whose original request (attempt.request) is a speed request, is refused unless it includes a measured stage timeline, the same as a fresh speed request. Acceptance: (1) a test where the new request text is a bare retry and attempt.request is the speed request from job 20261025-190606-eebk, built from that job's recorded request, asserts the reading is refused for lacking a timeline; (2) the same retry with a measured stage timeline in the reading is accepted; (3) a fresh speed request is still refused or accepted as before; (4) a non-speed retry is not refused; (5) the changelog states which of the three cited jobs (including 20261025-190606-eebk) the rule now refuses, checked by running the rule over each one's recorded request.
